steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Specialisation means focusing on producing a limited range of goods or services — individuals, firms, and countries can all specialise. | Key Fact: Division of labour breaks production into separate tasks, with each worker performing one task. Adam Smith identified this as a key source of productivity gains. | Key Fact: Benefits: increased productivity, time saved (no switching tasks), specialist equipment, higher output and lower unit costs. | Key Fact: Costs: worker boredom and demotivation, over-dependence on one product or market, skills become obsolete if the industry changes.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain three benefits and two costs of the division of labour for workers and firms. | Analyse why specialisation leads to exchange and interdependence. | Evaluate whether the benefits of specialisation always outweigh the costs.
